concerns.text: FR-004 requires a two‑sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test and a permutation test. Both assume that the samples (event‑window anomalies and control‑window anomalies) are independent draws. In this study the pressure time‑series are temporally autocorrelated and many earthquakes share the same geographic location, so the anomaly values are not independent. Using KS (or a simple label‑shuffling permutation) without accounting for this dependence can inflate type‑I error rates, making the validation of the association unsound.

SC-001 states that the association strength (Cohen’s d) and significance (p‑value) are measured against the null hypothesis of no difference between event and control windows. This is a definition of hypothesis testing rather than a measurable outcome; it cannot be false. The success criterion should specify a concrete target (e.g., “detect a Cohen’s d ≥ 0.3 with p < 0.05 in at least 80 % of bootstrap resamples”) rather than restating the null hypothesis.
